key_insight: B-site antisite disorder in Sr2FeRuO6 supports a Griffiths-like magnetic phase with short-range ferromagnetic clusters alongside strongly localized charge transport.
engineering_relevance: The findings inform disorder-aware design of magnetic oxides for potential spintronic applications, rather than AI or solar-cell engineering.
method: Structural characterization of monoclinic Sr2FeRuO6 and B-site antisite disorder.
Magnetic measurements probing ordering and short-range ferromagnetic clusters.
Temperature-dependent transport analysis of small-polaron and variable-range hopping.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a Griffiths phase extending well above the magnetic ordering temperature and transport changing from small-polaron hopping at high temperatures to variable-range hopping at intermediate temperatures.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative performance metrics or device validation, so practical spintronic benefits remain unestablished.
paper_title: Disorder-Induced Griffiths like Phase and Charge Localization in Sr2FeRuO6
